findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: (REPEAT X2) The PIC is not currently a CFPM and is missing critical food safety knowledge at the time of this inspection. Education was given in relation to the observed violations and concerns noted during this inspection. More knowledge is needed and would normally be covered by the CFPM course that is required. While education will be deemed as sufficient at this time other enforcement is likely if this becomes an ongoing issue.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(1) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE (PIC) shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: (REPEAT X2) On arrival, there is not a CFPM available in the facility. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all food handling shifts in the facility moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: (REPEAT X1) A bucket full of spout covers was observed to be stored in front of the handwashing sink at the bar. CORRECTED: Education was conducted. The bucket was relocated making the handwashing sink accessible. Ensure that all sinks within the facility designated for handwashing are accessible for handwashing at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution in the triple sink inside the kitchen tested below the manufacturer’s recommended concentration at 100ppm instead of between 200-400ppm. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and emptied the triple sink and remade it and it tested between 200-400ppm. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are prepared as directed by the EPA regulation label with a concentration between 200-400ppm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of soil residues in the rubber holders of the soda nozzles at both bars. PIC was informed and staff will clean the rubber holders. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple open jars of Butch’s All Purpose hot sauce/marinade stored in the dry storage areas. According to the sauces packaging, these jars require refrigeration after opening. Ensure all foods that require cold holding are stored at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the open jars of sauce.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: (REPEAT X1) Inspectors observed a carton of heavy whipping cream in the reach in cooler at the bar to not be date marked. An employee was asked when the carton was opened and they were unsure of when it had been opened. CORRECTED: The carton of heavy whipping cream was voluntarily discarded. Ensure that all TCS or RTE food items that are going to stay over 24-hours from the date they were opened or prepared are date marked properly at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed several fruit flies in the bar area near the handwashing sink. Pest control was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that the facility is maintained free of pests through regular pest control and cleaning frequently to avoid pest harborage conditions.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: A knife was observed to be stored under a piece of metal connecting the soup warmer and microwave. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the knife was removed to be cleaned. Ensure that in use utensils are stored in locations that are cleaned regularly. Inspector suggests using the magnetic knife rack or a separate cleanable container to store utensils properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed single-service containers on a shelf in the kitchen stored unprotected. CORRECTED: PIC was made aware and containers were inverted to correct the violation. Ensure that single-service items food-contact surfaces are protected by their original packaging or inverted to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: An accumulation of grease was observed on the wall behind the grill and flat top in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. Ensure that surfaces, equipment and utensils are cleaned frequently to avoid accumulation of soil and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the trash can in the women’s restroom to not have a lid. PIC was informed. Ensure that trash bins in bathrooms used by women have a covering.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following was observed:
1. The handwashing sink in the kitchen has a gap between it and the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to seal so that a smooth and easily cleanable surface is available at all times.  
2. The caulking along the handwashing sink and the wall in the mens restroom in the main area as well as both bathrooms outside was cracked.

Ensure that surfaces are maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a mop stored in the lower basin of the mop bucket inside the outdoor mens restroom. Ensure that mops are hung to allow mop heads to dry after each use.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed personal food items stored intermixed with food items intended for consumers in the mini fridge behind the bar. There was an employee’s meal stored in the reach in bar cooler above restaurant inventory. Ensure that personal items are stored in a designated area separate from items intended for customers.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: On arrival, there is not a CFPM available in the facility. The kitchen manager stated that they should be going through the process soon. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all food handling shifts in the facility moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employee donning gloves multiple times without handwashing. Activities were halted and education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees are reminded to always wash their hands before donning gloves including in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Upon arrival, a cluster of scrubs and other items were observed stored in the hand sink. Education was carried out. The items were removed making the hand sink accessible. Ensure that all hand sink within the facility designated for handwashing are use for handwashing only at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw pork chops stored over tomatoes and other ready to eat food items in the walk-in cooler. The kitchen manager was made aware. The pork chops were removed to be stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored in the appropriate order to avoid cross contamination at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer observed int he kitchen at the beginning of today’s inspection. Education was carried out. A sani bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm for quaternary ammonia. Ensure that there is always sanitizer made and available during food prep and service at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The following date marking issues were observed. 
1. A container of cooked and cooled green beans were observed without the adequate date marking in the walk-in cooler by the kitchen.
2. A container of cooked and cooled chess and potatoes was observed not properly date marked in the walk-in cooler next to the kitchen. 
3. A container of cooked and cooled brisket was observed without proper date marking in the walk-in cooler outside the building by the stage.
The kitchen manager told inspector that the items listed above were made yesterday but the person on shift forgot to date marked in them. Ensure that all food items that are going to stay over 24-hours from the date they were cooked or made are date marked properly at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
findings.comment: Inspector did not observe any sign of a consumer advisory present within the facility during today’s inspection. Education was carried out and a placard was provided. Ensure that there is a display of a consumer advisory visible for patron to see within the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a series of boxes filled with food items stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. The boxes were removed and stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored at least sis inches above the floor protecting food items from splash and other contaminations at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Allergen awareness notice
findings.comment:
There was no visible allergen awareness notice observed within the facility during today’s inspection. A copy was provided for correction. Ensure that the allergen awareness is posted and visible for customers at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(1) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE (PIC) shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. 

The PIC is not currently a CFPM and is missing critical food safety knowledge at the time of this inspection. Education was given in relation to the observed violations and concerns noted during this inspection. More knowledge is needed and would normally be covered by the CFPM course that is required. While education will be deemed as sufficient at this time other enforcement is likely if this becomes an ongoing issue.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there is not a CFPM available in the facility. The kitchen manager stated that they should be going through the process soon. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all food handling shifts in the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen would not dispense paper towels. Investigation showed that the towels were not fed into the equipment correctly. The PIC was unable to get the equipment functioning correctly. A set of paper towels were set out for hand washing to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are fully and correctly supplied at all times. Paper towels not being accessible is a repeat situation for this location from the previous routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

A brown lumpy substance was observed on ice in the ice machine. The only location this could have come from is the equipment. The kitchen manager was shown and discarded the ice to correct. Ensure that the food contact equipment in the facility is cleaned and sanitized often enough to prevent contaminants from reaching foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The fry slicer is observed soiled at the time of this inspection. The PIC indicated that the equipment had not yet been used for today. This means that it was left overnight soiled. The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours. 

A half pan of cooked hamburgers was observed on the front of the grill with internal temperatures of 56F. The pan is not on a hot element for the equipment. The kitchen manager stated that they were letting the items warm up before they would get an order to cook them. This is not a safe practice and would allow for temperature abuse of TCS foods. Education was conducted and the pan moved back to dish to correct. Cease this process immediately. Keep all TCS foods either above 135F or below 41F with a quick change between to the two temperature ranges.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A-E) Time/Temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

On arrival a full pan of fish is observed thawing at room temperature. Education was conducted. The PIC placed the pan into the walk in cooler during this inspection to correct. Ensure that thawing takes place correctly at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival and throughout the first part of the inspection there was not a sanitizer prepared for use in the bar area. Drinks are being served. The bartender was consulted and prepared a bucket to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use at all times that foods and food contact surfaces are being handled in the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The three employees at the facility are without reporting agreements or other versions at the time of this inspection. Clean copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement were given and filled out during this inspection to correct. Ensure that reporting agreements are maintained for all food handlers at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen was without paper towels. The PIC refilled the dispenser during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are fully and correctly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The fry slicer is observed soiled at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several fruit flies/gnats are observed in the vicinity of the fry slicer in the kitchen during this inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact pest control for maintenance. A follow-up is being scheduled for 10 days to ensure that the situation has been brought into compliance.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The fry slicer is observed soiled at the time of this inspection. 2) Multiple knives on the magnetic strip are observed soiled during this inspection. This inspection is being conducted as initial prep is about to begin and these items are stored this way since last night, indicating that sufficient cleaning did not take place. The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

A pan of cooked beef is observed with a date of 3-3 in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and stated that it was from last night and was mislabeled by accident. The items appear new and were allowed to be relabeled to correct. Insure that all date marking is done correctly at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of this inspection none of the current certified food protection managers (CFPMs) have an available allergen training certificate observable. Ensure that all CFPMs have completed allergen training and maintain copies of the certificate at this facility moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.15: FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes. 

The drain line coming out of the walk in cooler drains into and drips into the sink used for thawing of foods. This poses a contamination concern of thawing foods and should be fixed immediately. The issue was discussed and a follow up set for 10 days for compliance. It is suggested that extra piping/tubing to the floor drain is likely to be the best option for compliance.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Allergen training is not available for the CFPMs in the facility. A hand out was given and explained to the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all CFPMs have completed an ANSI accredited allergen training course prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

The item was shown to the kitchen manager and moved to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

The kitchen manger stated that they are from this previous Saturday (St. Patrick’s Day) and were to be discarded today. Ensure that all RTE TCS foods are dated at the end of shift each day and that date marking procedures are followed. The items were discarded to correct.

The steam table used for buffet style service is observed with food debris still on it from the previous event. Maintain these items clean at all times.

findings.comment:

findings.comment:

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

On arrival, raw chicken is observed thawing in standing water in the kitchen’s large sink. A conversation took place in relation to thawing practices and it is suggested to place chicken (or other thawing foods) in a cleaned/sanitized bucket that would allow water to flow into it, overflow and then drain. Chicken was moved during this inspection to correct.

(C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

During this inspection the tube is in contact with the standing water that is containing thawing chicken (refer to line item 35). This is a potential source of cross contamination and should be managed. The tube was removed from the sink to correct the violation. If it is non-functioning it is suggested to remove the item.

findings.comment:
Floors of the kitchen and in the walk-in cooler observed to have an accumulation of soil build up around equipment. Clean under equipment routinely.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
